extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and USPTO examiners (users of the MPEP)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on determining, calculating, preserving, contesting, and reinstating patent term adjustment (PTA) under 35 U.S.C. 154(b) and 37 CFR 1.703–1.705, including safe harbors, continuing-application rules, required filings, and office procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to provide application in condition for examination (37 CFR 1.704(c)(13))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there is a failure to provide an application in condition for examination within eight months from the filing date under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) or the commencement of the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371(b)/(f), the period of adjustment set forth in 37 CFR 1.703 shall be reduced by the number of days beginning the day after that eight-month date and ending on the date the application is in condition for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines a concrete 8-month trigger; reduction equals the days between day after 8-month deadline and the date application becomes in condition for examination (see 37 CFR 1.704(f) for what 'in condition' means). Use this to calculate reductions under 1.703.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecution via a continuing application constitutes failure to engage in reasonable efforts (37 CFR 1.704(c)(14))
rubrics_metrics.description: Further prosecution via a continuing application is a circumstance that constitutes a failure of an applicant to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude processing or examination of an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains types of continuing applications (continuation, divisional, continuation-in-part) and that applicants should not expect PTA from periods prior to the actual filing date of the application that resulted in the patent; cites Mohsenzadeh v. Lee and clarifies that PTA does not carry over to continuing or divisional applications. For CPAs, PTA will not include any period prior to the CPA request filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPA entitlement and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: A CPA under 37 CFR 1.53(d) filed on or after May 29, 2000 and before July 14, 2003 is entitled to PTA provisions as amended, but the period of PTA will not include any period prior to the filing date of the request for that CPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes design-application restrictions (CPAs only in design apps on/after July 14, 2003 and design apps not entitled to PTA) and emphasizes that periods before the filing date are irrelevant to PTA entitlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-application delays not relevant to PTA
rubrics_metrics.description: Delays before the filing date of an application are not relevant to whether an application is entitled to PTA; PTA will not be reduced by applicant actions/inactions occurring in a prior (or other) application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that applicant conduct in a different prior application generally should not reduce PTA in the later-filed application that resulted in the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS safe harbor conditions (37 CFR 1.704(d)(1)(i) and (ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: An information disclosure statement (IDS) in compliance with 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98 will not be considered (i.e., will not result in a reduction) under certain 1.704(c) provisions if accompanied by a statement that each item: (i) was first cited in any communication from a patent office in a counterpart foreign/international application or from the Office and that communication was not received by any individual designated in 37 CFR 1.56(c) more than 30 days prior to filing the IDS; or (ii) is a communication issued by a patent office in a counterpart foreign/international application or by the Office and was not received by any individual designated in 37 CFR 1.56(c) more than 30 days prior to the filing of the IDS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes the two alternative 30-day safe-harbor predicates; compliance protects against reductions under 1.704(c)(6),(8),(9),(10) (and related provisions). The 30-day period is strictly enforced and non-extendable.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE consisting only of an IDS with safe harbor statement not a failure (37 CFR 1.704(d)(1) amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for continued examination (RCE) filed in compliance with 37 CFR 1.114 that contains no submission other than an IDS in compliance with 1.97/1.98 will not be considered a failure to engage in reasonable efforts under 37 CFR 1.704(c)(12), if accompanied by the statement provided for in 37 CFR 1.704(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits RCE filings that are only IDSs (with proper safe-harbor statement) without triggering PTA-reducing failure findings; see final rule Changes to Patent Term Adjustment (Jan 9, 2015).

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe harbor statement must be filed concurrently with IDS (same date)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.704(d)(1) requires that the safe harbor statement be filed 'accompanied by' the IDS — i.e., filed concurrently on the same date as the IDS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the statement is not filed on the same date, applicant should consider filing a request for reconsideration of PTA (37 CFR 1.705(b)) along with a 37 CFR 1.183 petition to accept the late-filed statement; IDSs filed more than 30 days after the relevant communication will not be treated as within safe harbor and the 30-day period is not extendable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for late-filed safe-harbor statements (37 CFR 1.183 petition)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office provides a procedure to seek a waiver via a 37 CFR 1.183 petition to allow acceptance of a late-filed safe harbor statement under 37 CFR 1.704(d), but a statement filed more than 30 days after the applicable communication will not be treated as filed within the safe harbor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may also file a request for reconsideration of PTA under 1.705(b) with a 1.183 petition and fee; the 30-day window is absolute and not extendable per 1.704(d)(2). A petition under 1.183 may only request acceptance of the late-filed statement, not extend the 30-day window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form PTO/SB/133 and document code requirements (37 CFR 1.704(d)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: To aid recognition of compliant safe harbor statements, the Office created form PTO/SB/133 'Patent Term Adjustment Statement under 37 CFR 1.704(d)'; safe harbor statements filed on/after July 17, 2023 must be submitted on PTO/SB/133 using document code PTA.IDS. Use of PTO/SB/133 (and PTA.IDS) indicates the form text has not been altered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form use was not required before July 17, 2023. Applicants may not alter pre-printed text; signing/submitting the form constitutes a certification under 37 CFR 11.18(b). Submissions not using the form or PTA.IDS on/after July 17, 2023 will be treated as if no safe harbor statement had been filed unless a timely reconsideration under 1.705(b) establishes otherwise. When the PTO recognizes PTO/SB/133 with PTA.IDS, the PTA calculation will take the safe harbor into account automatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not alter PTO/SB/133 and correct document codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may not alter the pre-printed text of form PTO/SB/133; using document code PTA.IDS on or after July 17, 2023 is a representation that the applicant filed the unaltered form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Altering the form or using PTA.IDS improperly can result in the Office treating the submission as if no safe harbor statement was filed. If filing outside Patent Center, inclusion of PTA.IDS on PTO/SB/133 satisfies the 'using appropriate document code' requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.56(c) — who counts as a designated individual
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals associated with filing/prosecution within the meaning of 37 CFR 1.56 include: (1) each inventor named; (2) each attorney/agent who prepares or prosecutes the application; (3) every other person substantively involved in preparation or prosecution and associated with the inventor, assignee, or obligated assignee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether foreign counsel is 'designated' depends on the role they play (substantive involvement). The date the designated person first received a communication controls the 30-day safe-harbor calculation; MPEP provides detailed examples (A–C) to illustrate application of the rule in various fact patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples illustrating 30-day safe-harbor computation and foreign counsel roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Concrete fact patterns where foreign counsel either is or is not considered a person under 1.56(c), showing how the 30-day period is computed from either the date the foreign counsel received the communication or the date U.S. counsel received it depending on whether foreign counsel is substantively involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example A/B/C show: (a) if foreign counsel is substantively involved (drafts/edits/amends), the 30-day clock starts when foreign counsel received the communication; (b) if foreign counsel merely forwards copies under standing instructions without substantive role, the 30-day clock may start when U.S. counsel receives it. These examples guide whether an IDS filed later falls within the 30-day safe harbor.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.704(e) — requests for reinstatement under 1.705(c) not a failure
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission of a request under 37 CFR 1.705(c) for reinstatement of reduced PTA will not be considered a failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude prosecution under 37 CFR 1.704(c)(10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This recognizes statutory requirement that such requests be filed prior to issuance of the patent (see 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(3)(C)). Filing the reinstatement request itself does not trigger a PTA-reducing failure finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'condition for examination' (37 CFR 1.704(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) is in condition for examination when it includes: a specification with at least one claim and an abstract (37 CFR 1.72(b)); papers in compliance with 37 CFR 1.52; drawings (if any) in compliance with 37 CFR 1.84; any required English translation; Sequence Listing/Sequence Listing XML compliance (if applicable); an inventor's oath/declaration or ADS per 1.63(b); basic filing, search, and examination fees; any certified copy required by 1.57(a); and any application size fee under 1.16(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For international applications entering the national stage, analogous documents and fees under 1.491/1.492 apply. Papers/drawings/sequence listings that are corrected by the latest reply prior to the mailing of an action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance will be considered in compliance as of the filing date for PTA purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term adjustment notification timing and official determination (37 CFR 1.705(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent will include notification of any PTA under 35 U.S.C. 154(b); the Office shall transmit a determination no later than the date of issuance of the patent. A preliminary PTA calculation may be provided earlier with the issue notification, but the PTA indicated on the patent is the Office's official determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because statutory guarantees may not be fully calculable at notice-of-allowance time, the official PTA is the amount shown on the issued patent. Applicants should wait until grant to determine whether to seek reconsideration under 1.705(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on correcting PTA via letters or certificates of correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters from practitioners disclosing alleged errors in the Office's PTA determination will be placed in the patent file without comment; the Office will not review these letters or issue certificates of correction under 35 U.S.C. 254 or 255 to revise PTA except (1) to revise PTA consistent with a decision on a 1.705 reconsideration request or (2) to match the total PTA shown in the USPTO electronic filing system's calculation screen for the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patentees may instead seek reconsideration under 1.705(b) or file a terminal disclaimer; certificates of correction will not be used to revise PTA unless the limited criteria above are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration of PTA (37 CFR 1.705(b)) — filing deadline and required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for reconsideration of the PTA indicated on the patent must be by way of an application for PTA filed no later than two months from grant (extendable under 1.136(a)), accompanied by the fee in 1.18(e) and a statement specifying: (i) the correct PTA and the basis(es) under 1.702; (ii) the relevant dates per 1.703(a)–(e) and the adjustment per 1.703(f); (iii) whether the patent is subject to a terminal disclaimer and its expiration date; and (iv)(A) any circumstances during prosecution that constitute a failure to engage in reasonable efforts under 1.704 or (B) that there were no such circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-month period may be extended under 1.136(a) up to five additional months (allowing up to seven months total after grant). The statement of facts must be specific and cite statutory/regulatory bases (1.702/1.703/1.704). Office procedure section explains how to file and evaluate such requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement of reduced PTA for late replies (37 CFR 1.705(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for reinstatement of all or part of a period of adjustment reduced under 1.704(b) for failing to reply within three months of an Office communication must be filed prior to issuance of the patent; this time period is not extendable. The request must be accompanied by the fee in 1.18(f) and a showing, to the Director's satisfaction, that despite all due care the applicant was unable to reply within three months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office will not grant more than three additional months for each reply beyond three months from the mailing date of the Office communication. The showing requires demonstrating 'all due care' (a due-diligence standard). Requests under 1.705(c) must be filed before patent issuance and cannot be extended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office procedures for verifying and correcting PTA-critical records
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should routinely use the USPTO Patent Center to check accuracy of data entered in the Office systems (paper type and date of receipt). The date to be recorded is date of receipt (not mailing date). If an original paper is misplaced and a duplicate is filed with a postcard receipt showing the original receipt date, that postcard date should be used. For Priority Mail Express®, the 'date accepted' on the label will be entered into Office records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If errors are detected, contact the examiner or Technology Center customer service promptly to correct records before allowance/issuance so PTA is calculated correctly. This guidance affects which dates are used in PTA calculations and may prevent the need for later reconsideration.
